'''Catherine Elizabeth Heymans''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRSE}} (born 1978) is a British [[astrophysicist]], the [[Astronomer Royal for Scotland]], and a professor at the [[University of Edinburgh]] based at the [[Royal Observatory, Edinburgh]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.roe.ac.uk/~heymans/|title=Catherine Heymans|website=roe.ac.uk|accessdate=9 November 2018}}</ref><ref name="BoyleShanks2000">{{cite journal|last1=Boyle|first1=B. ==Early life==
Heymans grew up in [[Hitchin]], Hertfordshire and was educated at [[Hitchin Girls' School]].<ref name="The Comet">{{cite news |last1=Derrick |first1=Maya |title='I never thought I'd get quite this far!' - Professor on Astronomer Royal appointment |url=https://www.thecomet.net/news/prof-heymans-on-astronomer-royal-8017728 |access-date=26 January 2022 |work=The Comet |date=1 June 2021}}</ref><ref name="THE">{{cite news |last1=Matthews |first1=David |title=Interview with Catherine Heymans |url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/people/interview-catherine-heymans |access-date=26 January 2022 |work=Times Higher Education' |date=3 January 2019}}</ref>

She received a first class [[Master of Physics]] (MPhys) degree from the [[University of Edinburgh]] in 2000. In 2003, she received her doctorate from the [[University of Oxford]] for research, supervised by Lance Miller, and in collaboration with Alan Heavens, on [[gravitational lensing]].<ref name=heyphd/>

==Career and research==
She won a series of fellowships at the [[Max Planck Institute for Astronomy]], the [[University of British Columbia]],  the [[Institut d'astrophysique de Paris]] and the [[University of Edinburgh]].{{clarify|date=November 2018}} In 2009 she was awarded a starting grant from the [[European Research Council]] (ERC) and was subsequently appointed a lecturer at the University of Edinburgh.

Heymans is best known for her work on using the technique of cosmic [[weak gravitational lensing]] to learn more about the Universe. She led the Shear Testing Programme STEP1 competition<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.roe.ac.uk/~heymans/step/cosmic_shear_test.html |title=STEP: Shear TEsting Programme |website=roe.ac.uk |date=2007-12-05 |accessdate=2012-10-22}}</ref> and co-leads the lensing collaboration of the [[Canada–France–Hawaii Telescope]] Legacy Survey: CFHTLenS.<ref name="HeymansVan Waerbeke2012">{{cite journal|last1=Heymans|first1=Catherine|last2=Van Waerbeke|first2=Ludovic|last3=Miller|first3=Lance|last4=Erben|first4=Thomas|last5=Hildebrandt|first5=Hendrik|last6=Hoekstra|first6=Henk|last7=Kitching|first7=Thomas D.|last8=Mellier|first8=Yannick|last9=Simon|first9=Patrick|last10=Bonnett|first10=Christopher|last11=Coupon|first11=Jean|last12=Fu|first12=Liping|last13=Harnois-Déraps|first13=Joachim|last14=Hudson|first14=Michael J.|last15=Kilbinger|first15=Martin|last16=Kuijken|first16=Koenraad|last17=Rowe|first17=Barnaby|last18=Schrabback|first18=Tim|last19=Semboloni|first19=Elisabetta|last20=van Uitert|first20=Edo|last21=Vafaei|first21=Sanaz|last22=Velander|first22=Malin|display-authors=5|title=CFHTLenS: the Canada–France–Hawaii Telescope Lensing Survey|journal=Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society|volume=427|issue=1|year=2012|pages=146–166|issn=0035-8711|doi=10.1111/j.1365-2966.2012.21952.x|doi-access=free |arxiv=1210.0032|bibcode=2012MNRAS.427..146H |s2cid=24731530 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cfht.hawaii.edu/en/news/CFHTLens/ |title=News CFHT - Astronomers reach new frontiers of dark matter |website=cfht.hawaii.edu |date= |accessdate=2012-10-22}}</ref>

Heymans is one of the leaders of the [[European Southern Observatory]] (ESO) project Kilo-Degree Survey (KiDS). 
In 2018 she was presented with the Max Planck-Humboldt Research Award, which is worth €1.5 million and financed by funds from the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF). The award is presented jointly by the [[Max Planck Society]] and the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mpg.de/12407860/max-planck-humboldt-research-award-for-catherine-heymans?c=2249|title=Max Planck-Humboldt Research Award for Catherine Heymans|website=mpg.de|language=en|access-date=2019-12-17}}</ref> The award will be used to establish the German Centre for Cosmological Lensing at the 
[[Ruhr University Bochum]].<ref>[https://gccl-rub.github.io/index Homepage of the German Center for Cosmological Lensing at Ruhr University Bochum]</ref><ref>[https://news.rub.de/leute/2019-08-09-forschungspreis-britische-wissenschaftlerin-will-die-dunkle-materie-verstehen Britische Wissenschaftlerin will die dunkle Materie verstehen, Press release RUB, August 2019]</ref>

Heymans teaches on the [[Massive open online course]] (MOOC) at [[Coursera]] on ''AstroTech: The Science and Technology behind Astronomical Discovery''.<ref name=mooc>{{cite web|url=https://www.coursera.org/learn/astronomy-technology|website=coursera.org|title=AstroTech: The Science and Technology behind Astronomical Discovery}}</ref> Her research has been funded by the [[Science and Technology Facilities Council]] (STFC).<ref name=ukri>{{cite web|title=UK government research grants awarded to Catherine Heymans|publisher= [[United Kingdom Research and Innovation]]|website=ukri.org|location=Swindon|author=Anon|year=2018|archivedate=2018-11-12|url=https://gtr.ukri.org/person/7BF33D2D-B87B-4D10-B916-14ED6525AF7A|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20181112095312/https://gtr.ukri.org/person/7BF33D2D-B87B-4D10-B916-14ED6525AF7A}}</ref>

Heymans' first popular science book, "How to design a universe: the science of real and virtual worlds" was published in the UK by Bloomsbury Sigma in September 2026.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Heymans |first=Catherine |title=How to Design a Universe: The Science of Real and Virtual Worlds |date=10 September 2026 |publisher=Bloomsbury Sigma |year=2026 |isbn=9781399421447 |edition=1st}}</ref>

===Awards and honours===
The [[Royal Astronomical Society]] awarded Heymans the [[George Darwin Lectureship]] in 2017<ref name="ras">{{Cite news|url=https://live.newscientist.com/speakers/catherine-heymans|title=Catherine Heymans|work=New Scientist Live 2018|access-date=2018-11-08|language=en-GB|archive-date=8 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181108144455/https://live.newscientist.com/speakers/catherine-heymans|url-status=dead}}</ref> and the [[Herschel Medal]] in 2022<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Catherine Heymans |url=https://rse.org.uk/fellowship/fellow/professor-catherine-heymans-4153/ |access-date=2026-09-20 |website=Royal Society of Edinburgh |language=en-GB}}</ref>. In 2018 she was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh]] (FRSE).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rse.org.uk/fellow/catherine-heymans/|title=Professor Catherine Heymans FRSE |publisher=[[Royal Society of Edinburgh]]|access-date=2018-03-14|language=en-GB|website=rse.org.uk}}</ref>

In May 2021, she was the first woman appointed as the [[Astronomer Royal for Scotland]], and the 11th person to hold the post.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-05-27|title=Dark universe expert first female Astronomer Royal for Scotland|url=https://news.stv.tv/scotland/dark-universe-expert-first-female-astronomer-royal-for-scotland|access-date=2021-05-27|website=STV News|language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Heymans has a partner and three children. Her partner volunteered to do the major part of the childcare. In March 2022, she contracted [[long COVID]]. In May 2023, she was suffering from long Covid, but had been able to continue some research activities by working in half-hour spurts.<ref>{{Cite news 
 | author = Alex Blasdel
 | title = The dark universe: can a scientist battling long Covid unlock the mysteries of the cosmos?
 | url = https://www.theguardian.com/science/2023/may/02/catherine-heymans-dark-universe-the-cosmologist-battling-long-covid
 | work = The Guardian
 | date = 2 May 2023
 | access-date = 7 May 2023
 | language = en
 | quote = 
}}</ref>

With her colleague from Edinburgh University, Joe Zuntz, Heymans has performed comedy routines based on astronomy.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Eaton-Lewis |first1=Andrew |title=Double stars: The comedy duo finding the funny in astrophysics|date=8 January 2022 |url=https://www.scotsman.com/arts-and-culture/theatre-and-stage/double-stars-the-comedy-duo-finding-the-funny-in-astrophysics-3514992https://www.scotsman.com/arts-and-culture/theatre-and-stage/double-stars-the-comedy-duo-finding-the-funny-in-astrophysics-3514992 |website=scotsman.com |publisher=The Scotsman |access-date=3 June 2025}}</ref>
